summary:
We developed an interactive space mission game using Scratch, where players design, launch, and manage their own spacecraft. Players must make engineering decisions by selecting equipment while balancing limited resources such as budget, mass, fuel, power, and hull strength.

During the space journey, players encounter asteroids and use different weapons and defensive systems to survive increasingly challenging waves. They can also explore asteroid surfaces, scan for scientific discoveries, collect samples, and transmit scientific data.

Finally, players must return to Earth, where their mission performance is evaluated based on their achievements and resource management.

Our project addresses the challenge by turning complex space mission planning into an interactive experience. It demonstrates how engineering choices involve trade-offs and how careful resource management, scientific exploration, and strategic decision-making contribute to mission success.
details:
Our project is an interactive space mission simulator developed using Scratch. It allows players to experience the different stages of a space mission, from spacecraft design to mission evaluation.

First, players design their spacecraft by selecting equipment while managing a limited budget and spacecraft mass. Their design choices affect important resources and performance, including fuel, power, speed, and defensive capabilities. After launching, players travel through space and face increasingly difficult asteroid waves. They must use different weapons and defensive systems, such as lasers, missiles, spread shots, shields, and Nova Rings, to protect their spacecraft.

The mission then moves into scientific exploration. Players can scan asteroid regions, discover and collect mineral samples, and transmit scientific data back to Earth. Finally, they attempt to return to Earth, where their performance is evaluated through a mission score and additional bonuses.

Benefits and Intended Impact:
The project makes space engineering more engaging and accessible. It helps players understand that real space missions require careful planning, resource management, scientific investigation, and decision-making. It also demonstrates how one engineering decision can affect the entire mission.

Tools and Technology:
We used Scratch, a block-based programming platform. Our project uses variables, lists, broadcasts, clones, sprites, costumes, and backdrops to create its interactive systems. No additional hardware is required.

Creativity and Team Considerations:
Our creative approach combines spacecraft management, asteroid combat, and scientific exploration into one connected mission. We considered limited budgets, spacecraft mass, fuel consumption, power supply, hull strength, equipment performance, and mission objectives. We also considered our team's development time and programming capacity when designing the gameplay.
